messages:
lina_support: ACME prod hitting intermittent 503s + 95th tail latency spikes on their Dedicated pool eu-west-2-dedicated-42. Started ~08:15 UTC and correlates with an autoscale event. Customer sees errors across model variants.

lina_support: Quick summary we got from customer: requests succeed mostly but 1 in 20 get 500/503 and token latency jumps to 800-1200ms. Happening across sessions. They suspect noisy neighbor/GPU contention.

autoscale-bot: scaled up from 6 -> 8 nodes (policy: latency_burst) at 2025-11-12T08:13:14Z (event id: sca-4721).

omar_infra: Can you paste the pool id and a sample request id? I'll pull GPU metrics.

lina_support: pool: eu-west-2-dedicated-42, sample req id: req_0a9f3c2. Logs pasted below.

lina_support: ```
2025-11-12T08:15:22Z req=req_0a9f3c2 status=503 model=redwood-v2 size=192 tokens latency_ms=1178
2025-11-12T08:15:22Z server=host-12 container=runtime-7 error="failed to enqueue request: timeout"
```

omar_infra: pulling host metrics for host-12 and sibling hosts on same rack. Give me 10s.

mig-bot: MIG topology change: none detected since 2025-11-11T21:05:00Z. Current config: 1xA100: 1g.5gb + 2xA100: 2g.10gb (shared).

omar_infra: Host-level snapshot around spike (08:15):
```
host-12: sm_util% avg=72, p95=98, memory_util%=45
host-11: sm_util% avg=18, p95=30
host-13: sm_util% avg=65, p95=92
cpu steal% host-12=7.2, cgroup/io wait=4.1
linux-throttle-events host-12=43 (last 5m)
```

omar_infra: Observations: host-12 and host-13 both show SM saturation bursts at the same time window. That suggests cross-tenant bursts rather than single-slice steady load. Linux throttle events on host-12 could indicate cgroup CPU starvation for the container managing batching.

tom_oncall: I triggered a targeted repro against host-12 with a bursty load script (short horizon, small batch sizes to stress latency). Results: some requests queued on the runtime for ~900-1400ms when sibling MIG slices hit sm_util p95>95. KV cache hit rate dropped ~12% during bursts.

omar_infra: Can you attach the runtime logs around enqueue timeout? Look for queue depth, batch formation times.

tom_oncall: ```
2025-11-12T08:14:57Z batcher: queue_depth=12 batch_size=8 wait_ms=120
2025-11-12T08:15:21Z batcher: queue_depth=28 batch_size=16 wait_ms=380
2025-11-12T08:15:22Z runtime: enqueue_timeout error=timeout waited_ms=500
```

omar_infra: That wait_ms=380 + enqueue timeouts explains 503s. Root cause: transient sm saturation on physical GPU leading to slower per-token throughput -> batcher backpressure -> enqueue timeouts.

neha_cs: What's the recommended mitigation for the customer while we investigate? Need something we can tell them ASAP.

omar_infra: Short-term: (1) bump pool autoscale_min to keep extra headroom during their peak window OR (2) temporarily move them to nodes with dedicated MIG (no co-tenant slices) if available. Also reduce max_batch_wait_ms to lower queueing latency (cost tradeoff).

tom_oncall: I pushed a quick config change to reduce batch_wait_ms from 500->200 for their model route in the pool and added a transient autoscale min +1 for the next 2 hours. Will monitor.

autoscale-bot: updated pool eu-west-2-dedicated-42 autoscale_min +1 until 2025-11-12T10:20:00Z (change id: sca-mod-889).

neha_cs: Messaging to ACME: "we've observed GPU contention on some hosts in your pool correlated with autoscaling events; we've reduced batch wait and added temporary headroom while we root cause. If you'd like, we can provision an isolation option (dedicated physical GPUs / single-tenant MIG slices) — cost and lead time below."

lina_support: Customer responded: please do the isolation option, they're sensitive to tail latency for their SLAs. Asked for ETA on dedicated nodes.

omar_infra: Investigation notes: potential contributing factors:
- MIG partition mix on hosts may allow high-saturation tenants to impact neighbors when they do short bursty workloads (KV cache pressure + SM context switches).
- Host CPU steal + cgroup limits caused batch assembly thread stalls on host-12.
- Autoscaler added nodes but some requests landed on older, already-busy hosts due to routing timing.

mig-bot: detected short-lived cross-slice SM saturation event at 2025-11-12T08:14:45Z on host-12. Affected slices: slice(0,1). Severity: medium.

omar_infra: Next steps: (1) offer customer single-tenant allocation (we can reassign them to nodes with 1g.x dedicated slices) — ops ETA ~3h for capacity prep; (2) add runtime guardrails: lower default max_batch_wait_ms for Dedicated pools that have mixed MIG slices; (3) add autoscaler routing dampening to avoid routing to hosts that just had a high-saturation event for 2m.

neha_cs: I'll send the pricing and the ops ETA to ACME now and ask if they'd accept the 3h window.

lina_support: Thanks team — I'll keep thread updated with customer ack. If isolation accepted, create a follow-up ticket for ops to migrate and include a post-mortem with recommendations.

neha_cs: ACME accepted isolation option, requested start immediately. I created ticket OPS-4741 and CC'd billing for the transient charge.

lina_support: Closing loop: mitigations applied, customer moved to single-tenant MIG set, tail latency normalized in the monitoring graphs. Will file postmortem notes in incidents channel. :white_check_mark:
